purpose: Measure where Lean's existing last-layer cross-attention usage falls when the selected token sets change but sequence 11 masks barely move.
method: Replay the exact automatic indexed-position Lean reference. Observe, without modifying it, the author-returned mean attention probability per memory key from the final memory-attention layer. Verify the first 4096 memory position vectors equal the original dense single conditioning frame plus its temporal embedding; the pointer count identifies the existing tail. Report normalized total mass on conditioning tokens, other spatial memory and pointer tokens. When Lean records pruning for a latest dense memory segment, verify that its 4096 usage values exactly match the corresponding attention-vector slice and report that segment's total and retained-token mass at that read. No labels are used to select frames or compute the observations.
constraints: No model edits, attention interventions, re-detection, new threshold, adaptive gate, or inference-time labels. Two independent seq3 label-free engineering replays must exactly match masks and token/position receipts and reproduce observation records before the selected videos.
interpretation: Attention mass is an average over query positions, heads and batch in the final layer, not causal token importance; a large or small mass does not prove an ablation effect. The latest-full-memory mass is measured before that memory's later pruning and does not directly quantify the later pruned read. These four previously inspected sequences are exploratory; no generalization claim.
